affected_boundaries: Implementation annotation attachment to class members

observed_behavior: The configured semantic check rejected implementation annotations on the private payment-executor factory method.
expected_behavior: Named private class methods and properties can declare implementation links without exposing their boundary.
causal_mechanism: The named-declaration predicate accepted Identifier names but omitted the distinct PrivateIdentifier AST node used for #private members.

anti_pattern.structural_description: An AST eligibility predicate represented a semantic category using only one of its valid syntax forms.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Equivalent named member declarations receive different traceability eligibility solely because of private-name syntax.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Named private members retain implementation attachment under the same leading-comment and declaration-kind rules as public members.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Accept PrivateIdentifier alongside Identifier in the existing named implementation predicate.

applicability_conditions: Implementation annotations precede a supported class member with a #private name.
known_non_matches: Public and private-keyword method names already pass.
Detached comments and string markers remain rejected by the unchanged attachment checks.
confirmation_evidence: The differential regression passed ordinary and private-keyword methods but failed #work before the correction.
After the correction, private method, async method, static method and property fixtures pass.
regression_proofs: tsts/test/traceability-graph.test.ts: implementation annotations attach to private class methods and properties
